description: The contract can receive ERC721 tokens but does not implement the transfer or approval logic needed to recover them safely. ERC721 assets moved through recoverERC721 can become permanently locked.

THORChain_Router records static allowances for rebasing tokens while real balances change after rebase events. A pre-rebase allowance can later withdraw more value than intended, draining later deposits or causing withdrawal DoS.

The router assumes a fee-on-transfer token transfer delivers the requested amount to the aggregator. The aggregator receives less than expected, which can revert swaps, strand tokens, or force the aggregator to cover the shortfall.
Fee on transfer tokens transfer less tokens in than what would be expect.This means that the protocol request incorrect amounts when dealing with these tokens.

During certain upgrade migration timing conditions, a user could finalize a withdrawal on the old L1ERC20Bridge and then withdraw again on the new L1SharedBridge, enabling a potential double withdrawal.

The settle logic requires total collateral minus loss to exactly equal the token balance. An attacker can transfer collateral directly to the vault, breaking this equality and permanently blocking settlement.

submitExchangeRateData and submitSDPrice depend on quorum from trusted nodes. If trustedNodesCount changes during submission, the existing count is not adjusted and quorum may become permanently unreachable.

newRatio is calculated and compared with minIbRatio in settleAuction().However, if newRatio is less than minIbRatio, settleAuction() will always fail and there is no way for the bonder to cancel and get a refund.
MagicSpend.validatePaymasterUserOp checks each withdrawal amount against the contract balance independently. Batched UserOps can exceed the total balance and make later postOp calls revert.
The l1LegacyBridge is not assigned during L2SharedBridge.initialize(), causing deposits sent via the old L1ERC20Bridge to fail before the upgrade is completed.
BaseRewardPool4626 omits required ERC4626 functions and events, so integrations relying on the standard cannot safely use it as an IERC4626 vault.
Missing block.timestamp <= endTime allows sponsorship after endTime even though the reward unlock period is over. Funds can still be deposited but can never become valid reward allocations.

The contract does not properly check the return value of ERC20 token transfer functions, this can result in failed token transfers being incorrectly treated as successful, and cause transaction reverts for tokens like USDT that do not return a boolean success value.
updatePollAddress calls verifyNewPool, which rejects an already existing poolId. Valid pool address updates can therefore revert, leaving the pool address impossible to change.

add does not reject duplicate lpToken values so multiple pools can point to the same LP token. lpSupply uses lpToken.balanceOf(address(this)) which double counts the same balance and misallocates rewards.
Concurrent proposals for the same NFT index can overwrite an earlier user's JPEG lock schedule when finalized. The earlier user can no longer withdraw the locked JPEG, causing permanent loss.
updateAdmin accepts an address that is already an admin. Passing an existing admin can remove or corrupt that admin status, causing unintended loss of admin privileges.
The redeem function lacks a whenNotPaused check. Users can continue redeeming while the protocol is paused, creating state changes that bypass the intended pause protection.

Penalty settlement only considers the validator balance in ValidatorWithdrawalVault and ignores funds held in the related vault. Operators can be marked underfunded even when total available rewards are sufficient.
When _withUpdate is false in add or set totalAllocPoint changes without massUpdatePools. Other pools keep stale accounting and receive incorrect reward shares.

When putOptionsRequired is true, premium calculation depends on the current block time and nextFundingPaymentTimestamp. Users can time bond calls near funding updates to pay less premium than intended.
Total voting power is computed from total locked tokens while individual voting weights only track delegated amounts. The mismatch distorts governance thresholds and can make governance fail.

subtag: Does not match with Doc, State Update Inconsistency
description: Users who lock AURA and receive vlAURA get no voting power unless they explicitly choose a delegate. The docs imply locked users should have voting power but accounting only records delegated balances.

Owner removal can be replayed across chains because removeOwnerAtIndex lacks chain-specific validation and final-owner protection. The same index can point to different owners on different chains, potentially locking the account.
The sync function is not called after every operation that changes asset balances. Internal balances can become stale, causing later calculations or external calls to use incorrect asset amounts.
ERC721 transfer logic does not update the stored owner value after minting. The contract can report an outdated owner after transfers, causing inconsistent token ownership state.

addToDelegate increases totalWethDelegated but withdraw does not decrease it. sync can then understate WETH reserves and make lowerDepeg underflow, preventing the protocol from restoring the dpxETH peg.
When totalSupply is 0, handleFees does not update lastFee, causing an inflated time difference on the next fee calculation and minting excess fee tokens, diluting existing holders' value.
The Dopex curve swap path can compute minimum output with the wrong price helper, effectively producing a zero or incorrect minOut and leaving swaps without real slippage protection.

VaultLP computes withdrawable assets from totalCollateral, but when all WETH collateral is locked and converted to RDPX the reported collateral can be zero. Shareholders can be unable to withdraw compensation.
When putOptionsRequired is true, timeToExpiry is passed to option pricing after conversion. If less than 864 seconds remain before next funding, it rounds to zero and all bond operations revert.

The fee calculation tries to calculate a fee such that fee/(supply+fee) = %fee using a simple interest formula (i.e. no compounding), this lead to slightly less fee collected when fee are collected more frequently (small timeDiff) vs less frequently (big timeDiff).
The calculation divides before multiplying, so small intermediate values round down to zero. The later multiplication then uses zero and causes the final amount to be understated.
In fees calculation, division is being used in the midst of the calculation, not at the end of it.This leads to lost precision in fee amount (as solidity doesn't save remainder of division).
CrvDepositorWrapper relies on an infrequently updated Balancer TWAP; stale pool snapshots can produce inaccurate pricing and failed or sandwichable distributions.
bond automatically triggers reLP and is open to anyone. An attacker can manipulate pool price before calling bond, force reLP to trade at an unfavorable price, then unwind for profit.

The factory can change auctionMultiplier/auctionDecrement mid-auction, altering profitability; with extreme settings (multiplier=0, decrement=max), newRatio=0 and tokensNeeded=0, enabling settlement to drain all tokens.

Aura reward distribution assumes the full reward token amount is received. Fee-on-transfer reward tokens reduce the received amount, causing users to receive less or no rewards and breaking reward claiming.
Hacked owner or malicious owner can immediately steal all assets on the platform
If AuraLocker is shut down the lock-rewards path reverts. Users can only take the unlocked withdrawal path with a 20 percent penalty causing admin-induced loss.
AuraLocker rewardPerToken accounting can overflow when rewards are distributed against a very small or low-decimal locked supply, locking reward updates and forcing emergency withdrawal.
The Uniswap V2 reLP path removes WETH-RDPX liquidity, swaps part of WETH to RDPX, and re-adds liquidity with inaccurate calculations. The flow can revert or leave unrecoverable WETH dust.

If claimRewards is called without Options.LockCvx the contract can still transfer CVX from the user when depositCvxMaxAmount is positive. Since no locking action follows those tokens remain stuck without recovery.
ReLP assumes the protocol owns all liquidity in the Uniswap V2 pool. It can calculate lpToRemove from total pool reserves and attempt to remove more liquidity than it owns, causing reverts.
The ETH path in _transferOutAndCallV5 reuses the same msg.value for every item in a batch. An attacker-controlled target can receive msg.value repeatedly across loop iterations and drain router ETH.

The fee calculation is based on the totalSupply of the basket token. But some amount of the totalSupply represents the fees paid to the publisher/ protocol owner. Therefore the fees are "overcharged".
When all user locks are expired the kick reward uses only the last lock amount multiplied by expired epochs instead of the total expired locked balance. Users receive less reward than owed.
Strategy migration can fail because JPEG is blacklisted in the strategy withdrawal path. When the controller attempts to withdraw JPEG during migration, the call reverts and blocks the migration.
The fee calculation is wrong. It should only get divided by BASE and not (BASE - feePct)
StrategyPUSDConvex calls earned without passing the required account argument. The call reverts every time, breaking balance queries and dependent vault or farming operations.

roundUp uses a hardcoded 1e6 roundingPrecision. At realistic rDPX prices, a 25 percent out-of-the-money strike can round back to the current price, making the option in-the-money and breaking premium assumptions.
yVault.getPricePerFullShare scales the price per share by 1e18 regardless of vault token decimals. Non-18-decimal underlying tokens produce incorrectly scaled share prices.
Oracle prices are returned with 1e18 precision while multiple contracts assume 1e8 precision. The mismatch distorts calculations and can cause inflated values, failed transfers, or underflows.

The reward distribution index advances even when current funds are insufficient. A malicious user can send a tiny transfer to influence the next validator allocation and redirect rewards to a preferred pool.
If the LP token is also the JPEG reward token, newly minted rewards increase lpToken.balanceOf used as lpSupply. This inflates the denominator and dilutes rewards for stakers.

distributeOther lets anyone call notifyRewardAmount. This resets the reward period and re-spreads undistributed rewards over a new seven day window. An attacker can cheaply delay reward distribution for normal users.

The put settlement threshold is public and LPs can withdraw excess collateral before settlement. Fast users avoid losses, leaving remaining LPs with more loss and potentially draining vault liquidity.

The contract requires each asset balance to exactly equal _request.maxAmountsIn[i]. An attacker can front-run by sending 1 wei to the contract so the equality fails and the liquidity provider transaction reverts.

MagicSpend.validatePaymasterUserOp() and MagicSpend.withdraw() use the same signature. Malicious users can submit a transaction via the paymaster and then front-run with a withdraw() call, causing validatePaymasterUserOp() to revert because the nonce has already been consumed.
A malicious actor can snipe the mempool to bond as soon as an auction starts; because only the bonder can settle and the bond can't be burned for 24 hours, the auction and funds remain frozen.
Before the contract is paused, an MEV bot can front-run by calling addBid across active auctions. This can block later competing bids and prevent near-ending auctions from being overtaken.
distributeRewards lacks access control, allowing an attacker to call it before settleFunds. This can reduce operatorShare below penaltyAmount and cause validator loss.
An attacker can front-run a transaction that adds rewards to a past epoch by adding dust rewards to a later epoch. The victim transaction for the past epoch then hits the require check and fails.
Auction endBlock is fixed and predictable, so rational bidders can wait until the final block instead of participating earlier. This creates a front-running advantage for MEV searchers.
The oracle integration does not perform sufficient freshness checks before using returned prices. Stale oracle values can therefore be accepted by protocol logic.
JPEG'd reads Chainlink oracle answers without checking freshness or round completeness, so stale price data can be accepted for collateral valuation.
massUpdatePools is public and loops over poolInfo.length without a bound. As pools grow the updatePool loop can exceed the block gas limit and prevent reward updates.
_getReward iterates from epochIndex to tokenEpochs. If a user waits too long to claim the loop can exceed the block gas limit and make rewards permanently unclaimable.

The newRatio decreases over time without a lower bound. A malicious actor can wait until newRatio < ibRatio or near zero, bond and settle the auction, and effectively steal most of the basket's assets with minimal required collateral.
By bonding at a precisely chosen block that makes newRatio = 0, tokensNeeded evaluates to 0 and settleAuction() can drain the basket regardless of balances.

Bonding mints dpxETH with a collateral discount but deducts a fixed amount of protocol WETH instead of accounting for actual user input. Repeated bonding can drain WETH reserves and block future bonds.

Calculations round down and do not adapt when the contract lacks enough tokens. safeRewardTransfer can send less than expected while accounting treats the reward as paid which creates user shortfall and inconsistent accounting.

paymaster's _maxRefundedGas = gasLeft + reservedGas, without subtracting spentOnPubdata. This way _maxRefundedGas will be much larger than the correct value. paymaster will refund the used spentOnPubdata to the user

When handleFees is called, totalSupply and ibRatio changes accordingly, but for newIbRatio calculation tokens minted in handleFees is not included. Therefore, ibRatio is calculated higher than it should be.

subtag: Does not match with Doc, Implementation Error
description: In StateTransitionManager::unfreezeChain function call unfreezeDiamond instead of freezeDiamond on IZkSyncStateTransition(stateTransition[_chainId]) instance.
The mint() function redundantly includes a nonReentrant modifier, despite calling mintTo() which already has it, causing malfunction due to double reentrancy guard and blocking minting functionality.
A first depositor can manipulate vault asset accounting by donating a large amount before later deposits. Subsequent users may receive too few or zero shares for their deposited assets.
Adding _lpToken to a pool does not check that it differs from the CVX reward token. If _lpToken is CVX newly minted rewards inflate measured lpSupply and dilute existing stakers.
function setBondPercentDiv should validate that newBondPercentDiv is not 0, or bondForRebalance will experience division by zero error otherwise.

If all users burn their shares, the totalSupply becomes zero. Subsequent calls to handleFees() will attempt to divide by zero, causing the contract to revert and rendering the Basket permanently unusable.
A malicious publisher can set minIbRatio to an extreme value during an auction proposal, making the auction impossible to settle and locking all user funds in the basket.
The noContract modifier relies on contract code size and can be bypassed from a constructor before code is deployed. This allows contract-based callers to pass validation intended for EOAs.

Basket.initialize() calls approveUnderlying(auction) without guarding against an untrusted ERC-20 approve() hook, allowing reentrancy into initialize() to overwrite critical addresses (factory, auction) and hide the malicious token.

The function Factory.setBondPercentDiv() allows the owner to set the state variable Factory.bondPercentDiv to zero.If Factory.bondPercentDiv equals zero then the function Auction.bondForRebalance() will always revert due to a division by zero.

The function Factory.setAuctionDecrement() allows the owner to set the state variable Factory.auctionDecrement to zero.If Factory.auctionDecrement equals zero then the function Auction.settleAuction() will always revert due to a division by zero.
If a token transfers control to the sender during deposit, the vault can be reentered before accounting is complete. This allows share or balance manipulation during token transfer.
function createBasket in Factory should also be nonReentrant as it interacts with various tokens inside the loop and these tokens may contain callback hooks.
User state is updated after sending reward tokens. If the reward token has transfer hooks or is upgraded to ERC777 an attacker can reenter and claim again before state is updated.

Because bond is permissionless and automatically calls reLP, an attacker can use a flash loan to move the RDPX-ETH price before reLP executes. The protocol trades at the manipulated price and the attacker arbitrages the reversal.
redeem calculates returned RDPX from the user's share of vault supply instead of current market price. A user can deposit before a price increase and later redeem more RDPX than intended.
The current implementation of TWAV is based on a short observation period, making it susceptible to price manipulation.
Penalty recovery uses the minimum of operatorSD and poolThreshold.minThreshold instead of the full penalty amount. When operatorShare is much larger, most of the penalty can remain unrecovered.

THORChain_Router emits TransferOut with the original recipient even when a failed native-token send is bounced back to the vault. Off-chain accounting can record the wrong receiver and break protocol invariants.

subtag: Does not match with Doc, Incorrect Parameter
description: unlockInWeeks - unlockTime compares seconds even though the logic intends to compare weeks. The greater than two check becomes two seconds instead of two weeks so locks can be extended earlier than documented.

The StateTransitionManager contract lacks a way to invoke executeUpgrade() or upgradeChainFromVersion(), preventing forced upgrades of deployed STs in urgent high-risk situations and undermining the documented safeguard mechanism.
Several contracts inherit PausableUpgradeable but do not implement pause and unpause controls. The documented emergency pause mechanism is therefore unavailable for those contracts.

description: When minAmount is zero and _ethToDpxEth is true, the code uses getDpxEthPrice instead of getEthPrice to compute minOut. The resulting slippage bound is incorrect.

subtag: Invalid  Slippage Control / Missing slippage check
description: Reward tokens are swapped directly to WETH through a fixed path that may not have enough liquidity. Users can receive far less output when a better route exists.

D3MakerFreeSlot.setNewTokenAndReplace removes the old token from tokenMMInfoMap but leaves its index in priceListInfo.tokenIndexMap, so the old token is still treated as configured and cannot be re-added with setNewToken or setNewTokenAndReplace.
An approved M earner can keep earning after governance removes it from the approved list because disapproval does not force stopEarning or remove the account from totalEarningSupply.

A malicious undercollateralized minter can repeatedly call updateCollateral in a short period and compound penalties until principalOfTotalActiveOwedM approaches the uint112 limit, breaking critical minting and accounting functions.

The updateCollateral validator threshold can be bypassed because one compromised validator can reuse historical validator data to update a minter state, allowing stale collateral status to be accepted without the intended quorum.

A restricted ArrakisStandardManager executor can call rebalance with a malicious payload that steals accrued manager fees and deposits them back into pool liquidity, deleting value owed to the manager.

When a new module receives its first deposit, ValantisHOTModulePublic assumes only dust reserves and can send all supplied liquidity to the vault manager instead of accounting it as user vault liquidity.
A malicious restricted executor can exploit rebalance with rebasing-token reserve changes to mint shares cheaply and drain all vault reserves.
After an admin whitelists a new module, a malicious executor can call ArrakisStandardManager.setModule with malicious payloads and then withdraw through initializePosition to drain the vault.

Adding liquidity can revert because ValantisHOTModulePublic calculates the token amounts to pull from ArrakisPublicVaultRouter higher than the amounts the user sent, so valid add-liquidity transactions are denied.
ArrakisMetaVaultPrivate.fund lacks slippage protection, allowing an attacker to front-run a private vault deposit and force liquidity to be added at an unfavorable unbalanced price.
USDT-style approvals are unsupported because the swap executor relies on OpenZeppelin 4.9.5 approval behavior without forceApprove or first zeroing the allowance, so swaps using USDT can revert.
USDC rewards use 6 decimal precision, and frequent reward updates can round each reward-per-token increment to zero, preventing the intended weekly USDC distribution from reaching stakers.
When a pair is configured with the maximum fee, RubiconFeeController rounds the fee down and ProtocolFees then recomputes a different expected amount, causing otherwise valid swaps to revert.

The clone-with-immutable-args pattern lets forged calldata control the delegated implementation address; a selfdestructing implementation can brick vesting escrow vaults and permanently block normal use.
Launch.updateParticipation compares token amounts with currency amounts without normalizing decimals, so a payment token with fewer decimals lets users bypass maxTokenAmountPerUser.

When a user reduces participation, Launch.updateParticipation subtracts refundCurrencyAmount from userTokenAmount in _userTokensByLaunchGroup, corrupting token accounting and causing refund loss or DoS.
If a user mistakenly approves DnGmxJuniorVault tokens to WithdrawPeriphery, anyone can call withdrawToken or redeemToken and withdraw or redeem that user's junior vault tokens.

DnGmxJuniorVaultManager._rebalanceBorrow only handles the case where both ETH and BTC exposures breach thresholds; if only one asset needs rebalancing, the vault can remain unhedged and become liquidatable.

DnGmxJuniorVaultManager.harvestFees converts WETH fees into USDC and stakes them for the senior vault, indirectly increasing junior-vault debt and pushing borrowedUSDC above the borrow cap, which DoSes vault operations.
DnGmxJuniorVaultManager uses usdcPrice and MAX_PRECISION in the wrong numerator/denominator order when computing price-adjusted values, producing incorrect amounts.
WithdrawPeriphery._convertToToken computes slippage amounts in 6 decimals for every output token, so redemption to WETH or WBTC has ineffective slippage protection.
WithdrawPeriphery defines MAX_BPS as 1000 instead of the expected 10000, allowing user slippage parameters to be interpreted 10x larger than intended.
An early DnGmxSeniorVault depositor can mint a tiny number of shares and donate aUSDC to manipulate the share exchange rate, causing later depositors to receive too few shares and lose value.
DnGmxJuniorVaultManager._totalAssets does not consistently maximize or minimize NAV as requested; under some market states maximize=true returns a lower value than maximize=false.

Migrated withdrawals set an outer Portal gas limit of calldata cost plus 200000 and an inner CrossDomainMessenger gas limit of zero; withdrawals needing more than the effective gas budget become permanently bricked.
After Bedrock migration wipes L2CrossDomainMessenger successfulMessages storage, legacy withdrawals can be relayed again, enabling replay and double spending of bridged assets.
SafeCall.callWithMinGas does not fully account for EIP-150 and EIP-2929 gas forwarding rules, so a withdrawal can be finalized with less gas than specified and lose funds.

CrossDomainMessenger replayability is not guaranteed because SafeCall.callWithMinGas can leave insufficient post-call gas for the caller, causing messages to be marked or handled in a way that loses user funds.
CrossDomainMessenger undercounts gas for cross-chain messages, creating an L1/L2 intrinsic gas discrepancy that can make valid messages fail or be priced incorrectly.
Migration witness parsing can be halted by a malicious call to a nonexistent function in OVM_L2ToL1MessagePasser, causing ReadWitnessData to error until the data is cleaned.
L1CrossDomainMessenger reverts on low gas in situations where the portal gas check passed, so low-gas finalization can still fail and strand cross-domain funds.
The required gas limit during deposit transaction handling is calculated incorrectly, allowing a carefully chosen gas limit to bypass intended L1 gas burning behavior.
Long L2-to-L1 messages can pass callWithMinGas but still run out of gas during relay because baseGas underestimates the cost of long calldata, causing users to lose bridged funds.
ChiikawaToken.mint is public and lacks onlyOwner or any authorization check, allowing any address to mint unlimited CHIIKAWA tokens and dilute or steal token value.
BlackStar.receive lets anyone reset releaseTime by sending ETH directly to the contract, so an attacker can repeatedly send dust before expiry and indefinitely delay the owner withdrawal.
ChiikawaSticker.claim calls _safeMint before clearing canClaim[msg.sender]; a malicious ERC721 receiver can reenter claim from onERC721Received and mint multiple NFTs from one purchase.

IdentityStaking.release restores selfStakes or communityStakes after a slash but does not restore userTotalStaked, breaking the staking invariant and causing later withdrawals to underflow or strand released funds.

DelegateToken.approve lets an operator approve itself for a tokenId, and revoking setApprovalForAll does not clear that token-specific approval, so the old operator can still transferFrom after revocation.

CreateOfferer requires its local nonce to match Seaport contractNonce, but Seaport increments contract offerer nonces even for skipped invalid orders, permanently desynchronizing the offerer and DoSing future orders.

EvolvingProteus.depositGivenInputAmount and withdrawGivenOutputAmount route through _reserveTokenSpecified without calling _checkBalances on the final reserves, allowing operations that move the pool outside the required balance ratio invariant.

A first XDEFIDistribution locker can use a dust unit supply and direct reward transfer to make _pointsPerUnit extremely large, causing later lock or unlock calculations to overflow and freeze user funds.
XDEFIDistribution._lock calls _safeMint before totalDepositedXDEFI and position accounting are updated, allowing an ERC721 receiver callback to reenter before state updates and steal rewards.
XDEFIDistribution derives new tokenIds from points and totalSupply + 1, so after unlock and merge burn existing NFTs the same tokenId can be generated again and _safeMint reverts.
BendDAO YieldStakingBase stores minted shares from Etherfi or Lido deposits as if they were asset amounts, so getAccountYieldBalance misaccounts yield among NFTs sharing a YieldAccount.
BendDAO isolateRepay validates only that onBehalf is nonzero and not that it owns each NFT, letting a repayment against one loan corrupt another user's isolate borrow accounting.
BendDAO erc721DecreaseIsolateSupplyOnLiquidate clears owner and supplyMode but leaves lockerAddr set, so a liquidated NFT redeposited as cross collateral becomes locked and cannot be withdrawn.
BendDAO isolate liquidation subtracts the current borrow amount from totalBidAmout even though only the earlier bid amount was escrowed, so interest growth can underflow and lock the auctioned NFT.
BendDAO has no on-chain bad debt handling path when collateral value is insufficient, so undercollateralized ERC20 or ERC721 positions can leave suppliers unable to withdraw liquidity.
BendDAO YieldAccount cannot receive Etherfi WithdrawRequestNFT safe mints because it lacks onERC721Received, making Etherfi yield unstake requests revert and locking positions.

BendDAO executeIsolateLiquidate transfers the collateral NFT to params.msgSender without checking that the caller is the winning bidder, allowing anyone to claim auctioned collateral after the auction.
BendDAO botAdmin unstake and repay flows read yieldAccounts[msg.sender] instead of the borrower's yield account, so the bot cannot close risky yield positions as intended.
Badger LeverageMacroBase reverses the gte and lte comparisons in _doCheckValueType, so post-operation CDP validation can pass when it should fail or fail valid operations.
Badger ZapRouterBase stakes ETH into Lido using a low-level call and ignores the success flag, so Lido deposit reverts are not bubbled and later CDP logic can continue with missing collateral.

ThrusterTreasure.enterTickets only checks winningTickets[currentRound][0], so users can still enter after higher-index prizes have already been drawn and receive tickets with unequal prize eligibility.
ThrusterTreasure.claimPrizesForRound transfers each prize's full deposited amount for every winning ticket instead of dividing by the number of winners, overpaying winners and draining prize funds.

ThrusterTreasure.setMaxPrizeCount can change maxPrizeCount after prizes are configured, so claims iterate over a different prize count than the round was created with and prizes can be skipped or exposed.
ThrusterPoolDeployer has incorrect Blast gas claiming logic, causing claimed gas accounting or recipient behavior to differ from the factory's intended pool gas distribution.
ThrusterFactory.setYieldCut changes the protocol yield cut without first claiming accumulated fees for all pools, applying the new cut to fees accrued under the old rate.
Canto asD.withdrawCarry assumes CNOTE exchangeRateCurrent is scaled by 1e28 even though CNOTE uses 1e18 scaling, so maximumWithdrawable is understated and owner interest remains locked.
Canto Market buy, sell, mintNFT, and burnNFT functions lack slippage bounds for bonding-curve prices and fees, allowing users to receive worse execution than expected.
Canto Market reward accounting fails when a user buys additional tokens while already holding shares, causing previously accrued holder rewards to be lost.

Yield Witch.auction permits the auctioneer address to be zero, so collateral tokens that revert on transfers to address(0) make the auction non-liquidatable and let bad debt persist.

Yield Witch _calcAuction promotes the debt amount to the full vault debt when the proportional amount is below the minimum, which also moves the whole collateral instead of the intended proportional collateral.
Caviar Pair.buy transfers fractional tokens before pulling the ERC777-compatible base token, allowing a token callback to reenter while reserves are inconsistent and buy at a discount.
Caviar Pair.add quotes LP shares from current reserves in a way that can mint too few LP tokens for liquidity providers, causing losses when adding liquidity.
Caviar first depositor can manipulate the initial liquidity share calculation and break subsequent share minting, letting later depositors receive too few LP shares.
Caviar swap and liquidity functions lack deadline checks, so pending transactions can be executed later under unfavorable market conditions.
Caviar price calculations assume an 18-decimal price format even when the base token has different decimals, producing incorrectly scaled prices.
Caviar Pair.buyQuote can round the required input down to zero or too little for small trades, allowing free or underpriced fractional token purchases.
Caviar NFT wrapping and unwrapping lets attackers swap tokenIds without paying a fee and capture token-specific airdrops held by the pair.
Caviar Pair.price reads direct token balances for reserves, so attackers can manipulate the quoted price by transferring tokens directly to the pair.
